v-a: Investment Landscape
Which of the following is a real (physical) asset rather than a financial asset?
Equity shares of a listed company
A bank fixed deposit
A residential flat held to earn rent
Units of a debt mutual fund
Real assets are tangible, physical assets; shares, deposits and fund units are financial claims on an issuer.
Investment Landscape
A fixed deposit offers 7% a year while inflation runs at 5% a year. What is the approximate real rate of return?
Real return is roughly nominal return minus inflation: 7% - 5% = 2% (precisely 1.07/1.05 - 1 = 1.9%).
Investment Landscape
An investor quickly sells funds that have gained but keeps holding funds that have fallen, hoping they will recover. Which behavioural bias is this?
Herd mentality
Disposition effect
Home bias
Recency bias
The disposition effect is the tendency to realise gains early and hold on to losses too long, driven by loss aversion.
Investment Landscape
Fixing a long-term mix of equity, debt and gold based on an investor's goals and risk profile, and periodically restoring that mix, is called
Tactical asset allocation
Market timing
Sector rotation
Strategic asset allocation
Strategic asset allocation sets a long-term target mix and rebalances back to it; tactical allocation makes short-term deviations from it.
Investment Landscape
Using the Rule of 72, roughly how long will an investment take to double at 9% per year compounded annually?
6 years
9 years
8 years
12 years
Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 / rate = 72 / 9 = 8 years.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Which type of scheme lets investors buy and redeem units directly with the fund on an ongoing basis at NAV-based prices?
Closed-ended scheme
Fixed maturity plan
Interval scheme
Open-ended scheme
Open-ended schemes offer continuous sale and repurchase; closed-ended schemes and FMPs do not, and interval schemes allow it only during specified windows.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Under SEBI's scheme categorisation norms, 'large cap' companies are
The 1st to 50th companies by free-float market capitalisation
The 1st to 250th companies by full market capitalisation
Any company with market capitalisation above ₹20,000 crore
The 1st to 100th companies by full market capitalisation
SEBI defines large caps as the top 100 companies by full market capitalisation, mid caps as 101st-250th and small caps as 251st onwards.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
What is the lock-in period for investments in an Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS)?
1 year
5 years
3 years
No lock-in
ELSS units carry a statutory lock-in of three years from the date of allotment.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Which asset allocation rule applies to a Multi Cap Fund under SEBI categorisation?
At least 25% each in large cap, mid cap and small cap stocks
At least 65% in equity with no market-cap restriction
At least 35% each in large cap and mid cap stocks
A maximum of 30 stocks in the portfolio
A multi cap fund must hold at least 75% in equity with a minimum of 25% each in large, mid and small caps; the other options describe flexi cap, large & mid cap and focused funds.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
A liquid fund may invest in debt and money market securities with a residual maturity of up to
1 day
365 days
3 years
91 days
SEBI restricts liquid funds to securities maturing within 91 days; overnight funds are limited to 1-day securities.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
In India, a mutual fund is legally constituted as a
Company under the Companies Act
Limited liability partnership
Trust
Co-operative society
Mutual funds are set up as trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, with trustees holding the assets for unitholders.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
Which entity holds the securities bought by a mutual fund scheme in safe custody?
Registrar and Transfer Agent
Custodian
Asset Management Company
Sponsor
The custodian keeps the scheme's securities safe and handles their settlement; the RTA keeps unitholder records.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
What proportion of a mutual fund's trustees must be independent?
At least two-thirds
At least half
At least one-third
All of them
SEBI regulations require at least two-thirds of trustees (or trustee company directors) to be independent of the sponsor.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
Which statement about AMFI is correct?
It is the statutory regulator of mutual funds
It is the industry association of SEBI-registered AMCs and not a statutory regulator
It acts as custodian for all mutual fund schemes
It sponsors every mutual fund in India
AMFI is a self-regulatory industry body that, among other things, registers distributors with ARNs; SEBI is the regulator.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
Which body is the primary regulator of mutual funds in India?
RBI
IRDAI
AMFI
SEBI
Mutual funds are regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
An investor whose complaint against an AMC is not resolved satisfactorily can lodge it on SEBI's online grievance platform called
NDS-OM
ASBA
SCORES
CKYC
SCORES is SEBI's centralised web-based complaint redress system for securities market investors.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
If a dispute with a mutual fund remains unresolved after the AMC and SCORES routes, the investor can seek conciliation or arbitration through
The RBI Integrated Ombudsman
IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal
An AMFI appellate tribunal
The securities market Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) portal
SEBI's ODR framework lets investors take unresolved securities market disputes to online conciliation and arbitration.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
Under the AMFI Code of Conduct for intermediaries, which practice is NOT permitted for a distributor?
Passing back part of the commission to an investor as an inducement to invest
Disclosing the commission earned on schemes recommended
Keeping investor information confidential
Highlighting the risk factors of a scheme
Rebating commission to induce investment is prohibited; disclosure, confidentiality and explaining risks are expected conduct.
Scheme Related Information
Information common to all schemes of a mutual fund, such as details of the sponsor, AMC and trustees, is contained in the
Scheme Information Document (SID)
Key Information Memorandum (KIM)
Monthly factsheet
Statement of Additional Information (SAI)
The SAI carries statutory information about the fund house common to all its schemes, while the SID is scheme-specific.
Scheme Related Information
Which document is an abridged version of the SID and must accompany every application form?
Statement of Additional Information
Key Information Memorandum
Trust deed
Annual report
The KIM summarises the SID's key information and is issued with every application form.
Scheme Related Information
How often must AMCs evaluate the riskometer of each of their schemes?
Every day
Every month
Once a year
Only at the time of the NFO
SEBI requires the riskometer to be evaluated monthly based on the portfolio, and any change disclosed to investors.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
A mutual fund distributor's ARN (AMFI Registration Number) is allotted by
AMFI
SEBI
NISM
The RTA
After passing the NISM certification, a distributor registers with AMFI, which allots the ARN.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
What is the purpose of the EUIN quoted on an application form?
To identify the individual employee or relationship manager of the distribution firm who handled the sale
To identify the investor for KYC purposes
To identify the scheme and plan chosen
To identify the AMC's SEBI registration
The Employee Unique Identification Number tracks which individual within a distributor firm dealt with the investor, aiding accountability against mis-selling.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Two plans of the same scheme hold an identical portfolio, yet the direct plan's NAV grows faster than the regular plan's. Why?
The direct plan invests in a different set of securities
The regular plan pays exit loads to the distributor
The direct plan's expense ratio does not include distributor commission
The direct plan alone is exempt from stamp duty
Direct plans carry a lower TER because no distribution commission is paid, so more of the return stays with investors.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Which statement correctly distinguishes a SEBI-registered investment adviser (RIA) from a mutual fund distributor?
An RIA earns trail commission from AMCs
An RIA is paid a fee by the client and does not receive commission from product providers
A distributor may charge both advisory fees and commission to the same client
An RIA can sell only regular plans
SEBI separates advice from distribution: RIAs charge clients fees and cannot take commissions, while distributors are paid commission by AMCs.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
An investor wants to shift existing investments to a new distributor. Which statement is correct?
The investor can request the change directly; no NOC from the existing distributor is needed
The existing distributor must first issue a no-objection certificate
The units must be redeemed and reinvested through the new distributor
A change is allowed only after one year of holding
Investors may change their distributor by submitting a request to the AMC/RTA without needing the old distributor's NOC.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
A scheme has investments worth ₹250 crore, accrued income of ₹2 crore and liabilities of ₹2 crore, with 10 crore units outstanding. What is its NAV?
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
A scheme's NAV is ₹40 and it charges an exit load of 1%. At what price will units be redeemed?
Redemption price = NAV x (1 - load) = 40 x 0.99 = ₹39.60.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
An investor buys units of an open-ended scheme on a day when the applicable NAV is ₹50. Ignoring stamp duty, what price does she pay per unit?
Entry loads were abolished by SEBI in 2009, so purchases happen at the applicable NAV.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
Where does the exit load collected on redemptions go?
It is income of the AMC
It is paid to the distributor
It is credited back to the scheme
It is paid to the trustees
SEBI requires exit load (net of GST) to be credited to the scheme, benefiting remaining investors.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
A scheme's NAV is ₹20 before it declares an IDCW of ₹1.50 per unit. Other things unchanged, what will the NAV be after the payout?
An IDCW is paid out of the scheme's assets, so NAV falls by the payout: 20 - 1.50 = ₹18.50.
Taxation
Stamp duty of 0.005% applies on purchase of mutual fund units. How much stamp duty applies to a ₹2,00,000 purchase?
Taxation
How is income distributed by a mutual fund under the IDCW option taxed now?
It is tax-free because the fund pays Dividend Distribution Tax
It is taxed only when the units are finally redeemed
It is taxable in the hands of the investor
It is taxed only in the hands of the AMC
Dividend Distribution Tax was abolished from 1 April 2020, so IDCW is added to the investor's income and taxed accordingly.
Taxation
An investor has a long-term capital loss on mutual fund units. Against which income can it be set off?
Any capital gains, short-term or long-term
Only long-term capital gains
Salary income
Only short-term capital gains
A long-term capital loss can be set off only against long-term capital gains; a short-term loss can be set off against both.
Investor Services
Except for ELSS, a new fund offer of an open-ended scheme can remain open for a maximum of
30 days
15 days
45 days
7 days
SEBI limits the NFO subscription period to 15 days for schemes other than ELSS.
Investor Services
Within what time must an AMC normally transfer redemption proceeds to the investor?
10 working days
7 working days
1 working day
3 working days
SEBI requires redemption proceeds to be paid within three working days of the redemption request, subject to limited exceptions.
Investor Services
An investor submits a ₹5 lakh purchase in an equity scheme at 2:30 pm on Monday, but the money reaches the scheme's account only at 11 am on Tuesday. Which day's NAV applies?
Monday's NAV
Wednesday's NAV
Tuesday's NAV
The previous Friday's NAV
For non-liquid schemes, the NAV of the day on which funds are available for use before the 3 pm cut-off applies, so Tuesday's NAV is used.
Investor Services
An investor puts ₹1,000 a month through an SIP for three months when the NAV is ₹10, ₹20 and ₹25. What is his average cost per unit?
Units bought = 100 + 50 + 40 = 190; average cost = 3,000 / 190 = ₹15.79, lower than the simple average NAV of ₹18.33 (rupee cost averaging).
Investor Services
Which statement is correct for a mutual fund folio held in the name of a minor?
Another minor can be added as joint holder
The guardian is recorded as the first holder
The minor is the sole holder and a parent or legal guardian operates it until the minor attains majority
The minor can sign redemption requests from age 15
Investments in a minor's name cannot have joint holders; a guardian acts on the minor's behalf until majority.
Investor Services
The Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) combines an investor's mutual fund holdings across AMCs on the basis of
Folio number
Bank account number
Mobile number
PAN
CAS is generated by consolidating all folios linked to the same PAN across fund houses.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
A fund returned 14% with a standard deviation of 16% while the risk-free rate was 6%. What is its Sharpe ratio?
Sharpe ratio = (14 - 6) / 16 = 0.50.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
A fund has a beta of 1.3 against its benchmark. If the benchmark rises 10%, the fund is expected to rise by about
Expected move = beta x market move = 1.3 x 10% = 13%.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
If interest rates rise sharply, which category of fund is likely to suffer the biggest fall in NAV?
Overnight fund
Liquid fund
Ultra short duration fund
Long duration fund
Bond prices fall when rates rise, and the fall is greater for portfolios with higher duration.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
₹1,00,000 grew to ₹1,44,000 in 2 years. What is the compound annual growth rate (CAGR)?
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
Which measure captures the total volatility of a fund's returns, including both market-related and fund-specific risk?
Beta
Standard deviation
Treynor ratio
Alpha
Standard deviation measures total variability of returns; beta captures only market (systematic) risk.
Mutual Fund Scheme Performance
Why are equity schemes benchmarked against a Total Return Index (TRI) rather than a price return index?
A fund's NAV includes dividends received, and TRI likewise assumes dividends are reinvested
TRI excludes dividends, matching how NAV is computed
TRI is always lower, making schemes look better
Price indices are not published in India
Comparing a NAV that includes dividends with a price-only index would overstate outperformance, so SEBI mandates TRI benchmarking.
Mutual Fund Scheme Performance
For an index fund, tracking error measures
The gap between the ETF's market price and its NAV
The variability of the difference between the fund's returns and the index's returns
The scheme's total expense ratio
The fund's beta against the index
Tracking error is the standard deviation of the return difference between the fund and its index; lower is better.
Mutual Fund Scheme Performance
Which is the most appropriate benchmark for a gilt fund?
Nifty 50 TRI
A government securities index
Domestic price of gold
Nifty Midcap 150 TRI
A gilt fund invests mainly in government securities, so it should be compared against a G-sec index.
Mutual Fund Scheme Selection
A retired investor with a large corpus needs a steady monthly cash flow with limited risk. Which approach suits him best?
An SIP into a small cap fund
A lump sum in a sectoral fund under the growth option
Investing the corpus in ELSS
A systematic withdrawal plan from a conservative debt-oriented scheme
An SWP from a low-risk debt-oriented scheme provides regular cash flow while matching a low risk appetite.
Mutual Fund Scheme Selection
An investor wants to park money for about two weeks with minimal risk and easy access. Which category is most suitable?
Overnight or liquid fund
Equity savings fund
Credit risk fund
Long duration gilt fund
Overnight and liquid funds hold very short-maturity instruments, so they carry low interest rate and credit risk for short horizons.
v-b: Investment Landscape
Which best describes the 'liquidity' of an investment?
The highest return it can earn
How quickly it can be converted into cash without significant loss of value
Whether the capital is guaranteed
How lightly it is taxed
Liquidity is about ease and speed of conversion to cash at a fair value.
Investment Landscape
₹1,00,000 is invested at 10% per year compounded annually. What will it grow to in 2 years?
Investment Landscape
The risk that rising prices erode the purchasing power of investment returns is called
Credit risk
Inflation risk
Liquidity risk
Reinvestment risk
Inflation risk is the loss of real value when returns fail to keep pace with price rises.
Investment Landscape
Spreading money across many companies and sectors mainly reduces which risk?
Company-specific (unsystematic) risk
Overall market (systematic) risk
Inflation risk
All investment risk
Diversification averages out risks specific to individual companies, but market-wide risk remains.
Investment Landscape
A 25-year-old salaried investor saving for retirement 35 years away, with stable income, can generally afford
Keeping everything in a liquid fund
Keeping everything in fixed deposits
Investing entirely in gold
A higher allocation to equity
A long horizon and stable income increase risk capacity, so a larger equity allocation can be taken to target higher long-term growth.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Which is a key benefit a mutual fund offers small investors?
Professional management and diversification even with small amounts
Guaranteed returns
Freedom from all market risk
A fixed dividend every year
Pooling lets small investors access a diversified, professionally managed portfolio; returns are not guaranteed.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Investors in a mutual fund scheme are best described as
Lenders to the AMC
Shareholders of the AMC
Owners of the scheme's assets in proportion to the units they hold
Creditors of the sponsor
Unitholders beneficially own the scheme's assets pro rata to their units; the AMC only manages them.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
How can an investor exit a closed-ended scheme before it matures?
By redeeming with the AMC on any business day
By selling the units on the stock exchange where they are listed
By transferring the units to the trustee
No exit is ever possible
Closed-ended schemes must be listed so investors can sell units on the exchange before maturity.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Under SEBI categorisation, mid cap companies are those ranked
51st to 150th by full market capitalisation
251st to 500th by full market capitalisation
101st to 250th by full market capitalisation
101st to 200th by free-float market capitalisation
Large caps are the top 100, mid caps 101st-250th and small caps 251st onwards by full market capitalisation.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
A flexi cap fund must invest at least 65% in equity and
Must hold at least 25% each in large, mid and small caps
Must invest only in the top 100 companies
Is free to invest across large, mid and small caps without minimum limits for each
Must hold no more than 30 stocks
Flexi cap funds have a 65% equity floor but no market-cap-wise minimums, unlike multi cap funds.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
An arbitrage fund mainly seeks returns by
Taking concentrated bets on small companies
Lending to lower-rated companies
Exploiting price differences between the cash and derivatives markets
Holding physical gold
Arbitrage funds buy in one market and simultaneously sell in another, earning the spread with low directional risk.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
The entity that establishes a mutual fund, similar to the promoter of a company, is the
Trustee
Custodian
Sponsor
Registrar and Transfer Agent
The sponsor sets up the mutual fund trust and the AMC and must meet SEBI's eligibility criteria.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
Which entity typically processes investor transactions and maintains unitholder records on behalf of the AMC?
Custodian
Trustee
Registrar and Transfer Agent
SEBI
RTAs handle investor servicing such as processing applications, redemptions and maintaining records.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
Which constituent manages a scheme's portfolio on a day-to-day basis?
Asset Management Company
Trustee
Custodian
Sponsor
The AMC, through its fund managers, makes investment decisions within the scheme's mandate.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
What is the primary role of a mutual fund's trustees?
To protect unitholders' interests and oversee the AMC's compliance
To pick stocks for each scheme
To sell units to investors
To value securities daily
Trustees supervise the AMC to ensure it acts in the interest of unitholders and within the regulations.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
What minimum net worth must an AMC maintain under SEBI regulations?
₹50 crore
₹10 crore
₹100 crore
₹25 crore
SEBI requires an AMC to have a net worth of at least ₹50 crore.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
An index fund aims to
Beat the index through active stock picking
Guarantee the index return
Replicate the performance of its benchmark index
Invest only in debt securities
Index funds passively hold the index constituents in the same weights, aiming to match the index before costs.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
Unlike an index fund, units of an ETF are
Transacted with the AMC only at end-of-day NAV
Bought and sold on a stock exchange during market hours
Available only during the NFO
Never listed on any exchange
ETFs are listed and trade continuously at market prices, so investors usually need a demat and broking account.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
Why is a diversified equity fund usually considered less risky than a sectoral fund?
It spreads investments across sectors, so a downturn in one sector has limited impact
It guarantees capital protection
It invests mainly in government bonds
It never invests in mid or small caps
Sectoral funds concentrate in one sector and are hit hard if that sector suffers; diversification lowers this concentration risk.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
A large cap fund must invest at least what share of its assets in large cap stocks?
SEBI categorisation requires large cap funds to invest a minimum of 80% in large cap stocks.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
An investor wants equity exposure at low cost and without the risk of a fund manager's stock selection going wrong. Which product fits best?
A sectoral fund
A small cap fund
An index fund
A credit risk fund
Index funds are passive, typically low-cost and eliminate manager selection risk, though market risk remains.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
An investor began an ELSS SIP in January 2024. When can the units bought through the July 2024 instalment be redeemed?
July 2027
January 2027
July 2025
At any time
Each ELSS instalment has its own three-year lock-in from its allotment date, so July 2024 units are free in July 2027.
Mutual Fund Products for New Cadre Distributors
A Gold ETF primarily
Invests in shares of gold mining companies only
Invests in physical gold and tracks the domestic price of gold
Guarantees a fixed return linked to gold
Lends money to jewellers
Gold ETFs hold physical gold (and permitted gold-related instruments) so their NAV moves with domestic gold prices.
Scheme Related Information
Where would an investor find a particular scheme's investment objective, asset allocation pattern and risk factors?
Statement of Additional Information
Consolidated Account Statement
AMC's annual report
Scheme Information Document
The SID is the scheme-specific offer document describing its objective, asset allocation, risks and costs.
Scheme Related Information
The highest risk level shown on SEBI's riskometer is
High
Extreme
Aggressive
Very High
The riskometer has six levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High.
Scheme Related Information
A mutual fund's Statement of Additional Information (SAI) mainly contains
The daily NAV history of each scheme
An investor's transaction history
Statutory information about the fund house that is common to all its schemes
The portfolio of a single scheme
The SAI, read with the SID, gives details about the sponsor, AMC, trustees and other common information.
Scheme Related Information
Periodic portfolio disclosure by a scheme mainly helps an investor to
Know the guaranteed return of the scheme
See which securities the scheme holds and in what proportion
Find the distributor's commission
Check the investor's own tax liability
Portfolio disclosures show the holdings, letting investors judge whether the scheme is following its stated mandate.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
To sell mutual fund schemes and earn commission, an individual must
Pass the relevant NISM certification and obtain an ARN from AMFI
Register with RBI as a dealer
Only have a bank account and PAN
Register as a SEBI investment adviser
Distribution requires NISM certification followed by AMFI registration (ARN).
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Trail commission paid to a distributor is
A one-time payment when the investor buys
Paid by the investor directly to the distributor
Paid periodically for as long as the investor stays invested
Deducted from the investor's redemption proceeds
Trail commission is paid by the AMC from the scheme's expenses on the assets that remain invested.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Where can an investor see the commission paid by AMCs to his distributor for his investments?
In the scheme's riskometer
In the Consolidated Account Statement
On the stock exchange website
In the AMC's trust deed
SEBI requires the CAS to disclose the commission paid to distributors on the investor's holdings.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
A distributor recommends a small cap fund to a risk-averse retiree who needs capital safety, mainly because it pays more commission. This is
Prudent advice
Mis-selling
Rupee cost averaging
Asset allocation
Recommending a product unsuitable for the investor's needs and risk profile, for the distributor's benefit, is mis-selling.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Investment cheques for mutual fund purchases should be drawn in favour of
The scheme
The distributor
The distributor's firm
An employee of the RTA
Payments must go to the scheme's account; distributors must not accept money in their own name.
Performance of Mutual Funds
A growth option NAV rose from ₹20 to ₹23 in one year. What was the return?
Performance of Mutual Funds
A unit bought at ₹10 is worth ₹12 a year later after the investor also received an IDCW of ₹1. What is the total return?
Performance of Mutual Funds
A benchmark is used by mutual fund investors primarily to
Fix the scheme's NAV
Decide the exit load
Guarantee minimum returns
Judge a scheme's performance relative to the market segment it invests in
Comparing returns to an appropriate benchmark shows whether the fund manager added value.
Performance of Mutual Funds
Comparing the return of a liquid fund with that of a small cap fund is inappropriate because
They have different objectives, risk levels and investment horizons
Liquid funds do not publish NAVs
Small cap funds have no benchmark
Returns of mutual funds cannot be compared
Performance should be compared among schemes with similar objectives and risk, such as peers in the same category.
Performance of Mutual Funds
Two schemes earn the same 12% gross return on identical portfolios, but one has a TER of 1.5%. Approximately what return do its investors get?
Expenses are deducted from scheme assets, so net return ≈ 12% - 1.5% = 10.5%.
Taxation
For income tax purposes, an equity-oriented fund is one that invests
At least 25% in equity shares
Only in large cap shares
At least 50% in foreign equities
At least 65% in equity shares of domestic listed companies
Funds with at least 65% in domestic listed equity qualify as equity-oriented and get the equity capital gains treatment.
Taxation
Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on
Purchase of debt fund units
Redemption of units of an equity-oriented scheme
Switches between two debt schemes
IDCW received from a liquid fund
STT applies to redemption (sale) of equity-oriented fund units and is borne by the seller.
Taxation
Units of an equity-oriented fund become long-term capital assets when held for more than
24 months
36 months
12 months
6 months
Listed equity and equity-oriented fund units held for more than 12 months are treated as long-term.
Investor Services
Which of the following is mandatory for KYC of a resident individual making a regular (non-micro) mutual fund investment?
Passport
PAN
Income tax return
Credit card
PAN is mandatory for mutual fund KYC, apart from limited exemptions such as micro investments.
Investor Services
A Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) is used to
Invest a fixed amount from a bank account every month
Withdraw a fixed amount to the bank every month
Move a fixed amount periodically from one scheme to another of the same fund house
Transfer units to another investor
An STP periodically switches money between schemes of the same AMC, often from a debt fund into an equity fund.
Investor Services
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) allows an investor to
Invest a fixed amount every month
Redeem a fixed amount from a scheme at regular intervals
Switch the entire holding at once
Receive guaranteed income
SWP sets up regular redemptions, which is useful for generating a periodic cash flow.
Investor Services
What is the cut-off time for purchase applications in liquid and overnight funds?
12:00 noon
Liquid and overnight funds have a 1:30 pm cut-off for subscriptions, compared with 3:00 pm for most other schemes.
Investor Services
A switch from one scheme to another is treated as
A transfer with no change in units
A fresh KYC event
An IDCW payout
A redemption from the first scheme and a purchase in the second
A switch involves selling units of one scheme and buying another, so loads and tax treatment of a redemption apply.
Investor Services
A folio number in a mutual fund is
The account number allotted to an investor by the fund house
The scheme's SEBI registration number
The distributor's ARN
The investor's demat account number
All of an investor's transactions with an AMC are recorded under a folio number.
Legal and Regulatory Environment
Mutual funds in India are governed by
Banking Regulation Act, 1949
SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020
Insurance Act, 1938
SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996
The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 lay down the rules for setting up and operating mutual funds.
Legal and Regulatory Environment
An investor has a complaint about delayed redemption. What should normally be the first step?
File a suit in the Supreme Court
Raise the complaint with the AMC or its RTA
Complain to the stock exchange
Write to the RBI Governor
Complaints should first go to the AMC; if unresolved, the investor can escalate to SEBI's SCORES.
Legal and Regulatory Environment
AMFI's Code of Ethics (ACE) mainly sets
Income tax rates on mutual funds
The method of NAV computation
Listing rules for ETFs
Standards of ethical and professional conduct for AMCs
The ACE lays down ethical standards for the conduct of the mutual fund business by member AMCs.
Legal and Regulatory Environment
If an AMC proposes to change a fundamental attribute of a scheme, existing unitholders must be
Given an option to exit at NAV without any exit load
Required to stay invested for one more year
Charged a higher exit load
Paid compensation by SEBI
SEBI requires prior notice and a load-free exit window when fundamental attributes of a scheme change.
v-c: An investor refuses to buy a stock now at ₹350 because he 'remembers it at ₹200 last year'. Which bias is at work?
Anchoring is relying too heavily on an initial reference point (₹200) instead of current information.
A debt fund earns 9% while inflation is 6%. What is the precise real return?
Real return = 1.09 / 1.06 - 1 = 2.83%; 3% is only the approximation.
A retiree who is drawing regularly on her accumulated corpus is in which phase of the investment life cycle?
In the distribution phase investors draw down savings, so stability and regular cash flows matter more.
A balanced advantage (dynamic asset allocation) fund
Changes its equity-debt mix dynamically, often based on valuation models
Dynamic asset allocation funds actively shift between equity and debt according to their model or market view.
What equity range must an aggressive hybrid fund maintain?
SEBI categorisation sets 65-80% equity for aggressive hybrid funds; 10-25% is conservative hybrid and 40-60% is balanced hybrid.
A conservative hybrid fund invests what share of its assets in equity?
Conservative hybrid funds hold 10-25% in equity and 75-90% in debt.
A gilt fund with 10-year constant duration must
Hold mainly government securities with a portfolio Macaulay duration of about 10 years
It invests at least 80% in G-secs while keeping the portfolio Macaulay duration at 10 years.
A multi asset allocation fund must invest in
At least three asset classes with a minimum of 10% in each
Exactly two asset classes in equal proportion
SEBI requires multi asset allocation funds to hold at least three asset classes with at least 10% in each.
When can a mutual fund create a segregated portfolio (side pocket) in a debt scheme?
On a credit event, such as a downgrade of a security below investment grade
At the fund manager's discretion for any stock
Segregation separates distressed debt following a credit event so that existing investors share any recovery fairly.
The purpose of swing pricing in open-ended debt schemes is to
Pay a bonus to long-term investors
Make redeeming investors bear the cost of their exit during stressed conditions, protecting those who stay
Swing pricing adjusts NAV for large outflows in stressed markets so remaining investors are not diluted.
SEBI's 'skin in the game' rules require that
Distributors invest their commission in the scheme
Part of the compensation of key AMC employees is paid in units of the schemes they manage
Paying key personnel partly in scheme units aligns their interests with those of investors.
Excluding index and sectoral schemes, a mutual fund scheme generally cannot invest more than what percentage of its NAV in the equity shares of any one company?
SEBI's investment restrictions cap a scheme's exposure to the equity of a single company at 10% of NAV, with exceptions for index and sectoral/thematic funds.
Which of these is a 'fundamental attribute' of a scheme?
The name of the fund manager
Its investment objective and asset allocation
Fundamental attributes include the scheme type, investment objective and terms of issue; changing them triggers an exit option.
When an AMC changes information in an SID between annual updates, it typically communicates this through
Changes are issued as addenda, which are read together with the SID until it is next updated.
The Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is meant to
Replace the SID for legal purposes
Give investors a concise summary of a scheme's essential information along with the application form
The KIM is a summary of key SID information, provided with every application form.
Under current SEBI norms, how are mutual fund distributors compensated by AMCs?
Through upfront commission paid by the AMC from its own books
Through an entry load charged to investors
Through trail commission paid out of the scheme's TER, with no upfront commission
Through a share of the exit load
SEBI moved the industry to an all-trail model, paid from scheme expenses; upfront commissions and entry loads are not permitted.
SEBI-regulated Execution Only Platforms (EOPs) facilitate investor transactions in
Direct plans of mutual fund schemes
The EOP framework covers platforms that facilitate transactions in direct plans without giving advice.
During a bull run, a distributor shows a client only a fund's best 1-year return and hides its weaker long-term record. This breaches
The duty to present performance fairly and in a balanced manner
Selective presentation of performance is misleading and violates codes of conduct and SEBI advertisement norms.
A scheme has investments of ₹500 crore, cash of ₹10 crore and accrued income of ₹2 crore, with payables of ₹5 crore and accrued expenses of ₹2 crore. With 25 crore units outstanding, what is the NAV?
Non-traded debt securities held by mutual funds are generally valued using
Prices provided by AMFI-appointed valuation agencies
To ensure fair and consistent valuation, debt securities are valued using prices from independent valuation agencies.
Out of what can a scheme pay IDCW?
Only distributable surplus from realised gains and income
IDCW can be paid only from realised, distributable surplus, not from unrealised gains.
An investor redeems 10,000 units when NAV is ₹15 and the exit load is 1%. What amount does he receive (ignoring taxes)?
A scheme with net assets of ₹730 crore has a TER of 1.2% per year, accrued daily on a 365-day basis. What is the daily expense charge?
Annual expense = 730 x 1.2% = ₹8.76 crore; daily = 8.76 crore / 365 = ₹2.4 million = ₹24 lakh.
Capital losses that cannot be set off in a year can be carried forward for up to
8 years, if the return for the loss year is filed on time
Unabsorbed capital losses may be carried forward for eight subsequent years, provided the return for the year of loss is filed in time.
An investor switches from the regular plan to the direct plan of the same scheme. For tax purposes, this is
Tax-neutral because it is the same scheme
A transfer (redemption) that may give rise to capital gains
Regular and direct plans have separate NAVs; switching means redeeming one and buying the other, which is a taxable transfer.
In mutual funds, GST is levied on
Services such as the AMC's investment management fee charged to the scheme
GST applies to services like management fees and distribution services, not to the purchase or redemption of units.
An investor invests in a liquid fund at 11 am on Wednesday and the funds are credited to the scheme before the cut-off that day. Which NAV applies?
For liquid and overnight funds, valid applications with funds received before 1:30 pm get the NAV of the day immediately preceding the day of receipt.
On the death of a sole unitholder who had registered a nominee, the units are
Automatically redeemed and paid to the AMC
Transmitted to the nominee after the required documents are submitted
Transmission to the registered nominee takes place on submission of the death certificate and the nominee's KYC.
An NRI wants his mutual fund investment to be fully repatriable. From which account should he pay?
Investments made from NRE (or FCNR) accounts are repatriable; NRO-funded investments carry repatriation restrictions.
When a minor unitholder attains majority,
The guardian continues to operate the folio
The folio must be updated to the new major's status with his own KYC and bank details before further transactions
The units are transferred to the guardian
On attaining majority, a change of status is required; transactions are not allowed until it is completed.
A fund earned 15% with a beta of 1.5 when the risk-free rate was 6%. What is its Treynor ratio?
Treynor = (15 - 6) / 1.5 = 6.0, i.e. 6% excess return per unit of beta.
The Sortino ratio differs from the Sharpe ratio because it
Uses beta instead of standard deviation
Uses only downside deviation as the measure of risk
Sortino penalises only harmful (downside) volatility, unlike Sharpe which uses total standard deviation.
A fund with beta 1.2 returned 16%. The market returned 13% and the risk-free rate was 6%. What is the fund's Jensen's alpha?
A high R-squared of a fund against its benchmark indicates that
Most of the fund's return movements are explained by the benchmark
R-squared shows how closely returns track the benchmark; a high value makes beta and alpha more meaningful.
Which measure is most appropriate for the return on a SIP with many instalments on different dates?
Point-to-point CAGR on the first instalment
XIRR accounts for the timing and size of each cash flow, which suits SIP investments.
A debt fund has a modified duration of 4 years. If yields rise by 0.50%, its NAV will change by roughly
A debt fund's portfolio YTM best indicates
The approximate return if all holdings are held to maturity without defaults, before expenses
YTM is the yield on the current portfolio, assuming no defaults and reinvestment at the same rate; it is not a guarantee.
A credit risk fund must invest at least 65% of its assets in
Corporate bonds rated AA and below (excluding AA+)
Money market instruments maturing in 91 days
SEBI categorisation requires credit risk funds to invest a minimum of 65% in instruments rated below the highest grades, i.e., AA and below.
In the Potential Risk Class (PRC) matrix, a debt scheme classified as A-III has
Relatively low credit risk and relatively high interest rate risk
Relatively high credit risk and low interest rate risk
Relatively low credit risk and low interest rate risk
Relatively high credit risk and high interest rate risk
In the PRC matrix, A denotes relatively low credit risk and III denotes relatively high interest rate risk (higher Macaulay duration).
An investor expects interest rates to fall significantly over the next year. Which debt category is likely to benefit the most?
Bond prices rise when yields fall, and longer-duration portfolios gain the most.
A high portfolio turnover ratio in an equity fund generally implies
Higher transaction costs from frequent buying and selling
Turnover shows how often the portfolio is churned; frequent trading adds costs that can drag on returns.
A share trades at ₹500 and its earnings per share are ₹25. What is its P/E ratio?
A value-style equity fund manager typically looks for stocks that
Have the fastest earnings growth regardless of price
Trade below their estimated intrinsic value, often with low P/E or P/B ratios
Value investing seeks undervalued stocks; growth investing focuses on companies with high expected earnings growth.
An equity fund's top 10 holdings make up 60% of its portfolio. This mainly indicates
When a few stocks dominate the portfolio, the fund's performance depends heavily on them.
An investor needs no regular income and wants his wealth to compound. Which option should he choose?
Under the growth option, gains stay invested and compound in the NAV, with no periodic payouts.
When comparing two similar schemes from different AMCs, which factor is LEAST relevant?
Consistency of performance against the benchmark
Whether the NAV is high or low
A low NAV does not make a scheme cheaper; returns depend on percentage changes in NAV, not its absolute level.
Many active large cap funds have struggled to beat their benchmark consistently after costs. For a cost-conscious investor, this argues for considering
A low-cost large cap index fund
If active managers struggle to add alpha in a segment, a low-cost passive fund captures the market return efficiently.
An education goal costs ₹5 lakh today. With 6% annual inflation, roughly how much will it cost in 10 years?
Future cost = 5 x (1.06)^10 = 5 x 1.7908 ≈ ₹8.95 lakh; ₹8 lakh would be simple inflation.
An emergency fund is commonly recommended to cover
Around 3 to 6 months of household expenses
A few months of expenses kept in liquid instruments covers job loss or emergencies without disturbing long-term investments.
Which step comes FIRST in the financial planning process?
Establishing and defining the relationship with the client
The process starts with defining the relationship, then gathering data, analysing, recommending, implementing and monitoring.
v-d: Investment Landscape
An investor's 'risk capacity', as distinct from 'risk appetite', refers to
The ability to bear losses given income, wealth, liabilities and time horizon
The willingness to take risk
The past returns of the portfolio
The volatility of the market
Risk capacity is objective financial ability to absorb losses; risk appetite is the psychological willingness to do so.
Investment Landscape
A ₹10 lakh portfolio was set at 60% equity and 40% debt. Equity has grown to ₹7.5 lakh and debt to ₹4 lakh. To restore 60:40, how much equity should be sold?
Total = ₹11.5 lakh; target equity = 60% x 11.5 = ₹6.9 lakh; sell 7.5 - 6.9 = ₹0.6 lakh = ₹60,000.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
What is the minimum investment an investor (other than an accredited investor) must make in a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF)?
₹1 lakh per strategy
₹50 lakh per strategy
₹10 lakh across all SIF strategies, at PAN level
₹1 crore across strategies
SEBI's SIF framework sets a ₹10 lakh minimum investment per investor, aggregated across strategies at PAN level.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
Under the SIF framework, unhedged short exposure through derivatives is capped at
10% of net assets
25% of net assets
50% of net assets
100% of net assets
SIF strategies may take short exposure via derivatives without hedging up to 25% of net assets, which distinguishes them from regular mutual funds.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
A small cap fund must invest at least 65% of its assets in
Companies ranked 251st onwards by full market capitalisation
The top 100 companies
Companies ranked 101st to 250th
Unlisted companies
SEBI defines small caps as companies ranked 251st and below, and small cap funds must hold at least 65% in them.
Concept and Role of a Mutual Fund
An overnight fund invests in
Securities maturing in up to 91 days
Equity shares held overnight
Government bonds with 10-year maturity
Debt and money market securities maturing in one business day
Overnight funds hold one-day instruments such as overnight repo/TREPS, giving very low interest rate and credit risk.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
At least what proportion of an AMC's board must consist of independent directors?
Two-thirds
Half (50%)
One-third
One-fourth
SEBI requires at least 50% of an AMC's directors to be independent, while trustees need a two-thirds independent majority.
Legal Structure of Mutual Funds
The AMC enters into the Investment Management Agreement with the
Custodian
Distributors
Registrar and Transfer Agent
Trustees
The trustees appoint the AMC to manage the fund's money through the Investment Management Agreement.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
Which statement about the branding of a Specialized Investment Fund is correct?
An SIF must use the same name as an existing equity scheme
An SIF must carry branding distinct from the AMC's regular mutual fund schemes
An SIF is branded as a portfolio management service
An SIF need not be identified separately
SEBI requires SIFs to have separate branding so investors can distinguish them from regular mutual fund products.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
To distribute SIF strategies, a mutual fund distributor must
Only hold a NISM-Series-V-B certificate
Clear the NISM-Series-V-D certification
Register as a stock broker
Obtain approval from RBI
SEBI and AMFI require the NISM-Series-V-D certification for distributors of Specialized Investment Funds.
Legal and Regulatory Framework
Which category of investor is exempt from the minimum investment threshold applicable to SIFs?
Senior citizens
First-time investors
NRIs
Accredited investors
The SIF framework exempts accredited investors from the ₹10 lakh minimum.
Scheme Related Information
The offer document for each SIF investment strategy, comparable to an SID, is called the
Key Information Memorandum
Private Placement Memorandum
Draft Red Herring Prospectus
Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID)
Each SIF strategy is launched through an ISID that describes the strategy, asset allocation, risks and other terms.
Scheme Related Information
Which of the following is an investment strategy permitted under the SIF framework?
Equity Long-Short Fund
Leveraged Real Estate Fund
Cryptocurrency Long-Short Fund
Unrated Credit Opportunities Fund

SEBI-permitted SIF strategies include equity long-short, equity ex-top 100 long-short, sector rotation long-short, debt long-short, sectoral debt long-short, active asset allocator long-short and hybrid long-short.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
A registered mutual fund distributor who wants to charge clients fees for investment advice must
Register as an investment adviser and keep advisory and distribution activities segregated
Simply add an advisory fee to the transaction
Get approval from the AMC
Pass the NISM-Series-V-B exam
SEBI's IA Regulations prohibit charging advisory fees without IA registration and require advice to be kept separate from distribution.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
An investor who invests through a mutual fund distributor is allotted units of the
Regular plan
Direct plan
Segregated portfolio
Closed-ended plan
Investments routed through a distributor go into the regular plan, which carries commission in its TER.
Fund Distribution and Channel Management
Why do AMCs carry out due diligence on certain distributors?
To set the distributor's income tax
To decide the scheme's NAV
To ensure distributors follow conduct and suitability standards and to prevent mis-selling
To register distributors with SEBI as RIAs
AMC due diligence checks distributors' business model, track record and controls in the interest of investors.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
A scheme has net assets of ₹1,200 crore and 48 crore units outstanding. What is its NAV?
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
When a segregated portfolio is created, existing investors in the scheme
Are allotted units in the segregated portfolio equal to the units they hold in the main portfolio
Lose their claim on the segregated assets
Must pay additional money to stay invested
Receive the face value of the troubled security immediately
Existing unitholders get an equal number of units in the segregated portfolio so they share in any future recovery.
NAV, TER and Pricing of Units
An investor bought 5,000 units at NAV ₹20 and redeems all of them six months later at NAV ₹22, with a 1% exit load. What does she receive?
Redemption price = 22 x 0.99 = ₹21.78; proceeds = 5,000 x 21.78 = ₹1,08,900.
Taxation
Units of an equity-oriented mutual fund become long-term capital assets after a holding period of more than
24 months
12 months
36 months
3 months
Listed equity and equity-oriented fund units are long-term when held for more than 12 months.
Taxation
TDS on IDCW paid to resident investors (where applicable) is deducted by
The mutual fund/AMC before paying out the IDCW
The investor's bank
The distributor
The stock exchange
The fund deducts tax at source on IDCW above the threshold before crediting it to the investor.
Investor Services
An investor submits a purchase in a flexi cap fund at 4:15 pm on Thursday and the money is credited to the scheme at 10 am on Friday. Which NAV applies?
Thursday's NAV
Friday's NAV
Monday's NAV
Wednesday's NAV
For non-liquid schemes, the NAV of the day the funds are realised before the 3 pm cut-off applies, which is Friday.
Investor Services
KYC completed once through a KYC Registration Agency (KRA) is
Valid only for the AMC where it was done
Valid across SEBI-registered intermediaries, so it need not be repeated for each fund house
Valid for one year only
Required again for every SIP instalment
The KRA system lets an investor complete KYC once and use it with any SEBI-registered intermediary.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
Fund X returned 12% with a standard deviation of 10%; Fund Y returned 15% with a standard deviation of 18%. The risk-free rate is 6%. Which has the better Sharpe ratio?
Fund Y (0.50 versus 0.60)
Both are equal
Fund X (0.60 versus 0.50)
Cannot be compared without beta
Sharpe X = (12 - 6) / 10 = 0.60; Sharpe Y = (15 - 6) / 18 = 0.50, so X delivers more return per unit of risk.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
Credit risk in a debt fund refers to the risk that
Interest rates rise
The market index falls
An issuer fails to pay interest or principal on time
The fund manager resigns
Credit (default) risk arises from the issuer's inability or unwillingness to meet its payment obligations.
Risk, Return and Performance of Funds
An equity fund with a beta of 0.8 is typically considered
Aggressive, moving more than the market
Uncorrelated with the market
Risk-free
Defensive, tending to move less than the market
A beta below 1 means the fund is expected to rise or fall less than the market.
Mutual Fund Scheme Performance
Under two-tier benchmarking, the first-tier benchmark of an open-ended scheme
Is chosen freely by each fund manager every year
Reflects the category of the scheme and is common to schemes in that category
Must always be a debt index
Is the AMC's own NAV
Tier 1 benchmarks reflect the scheme category, enabling like-for-like comparison; tier 2 can reflect the fund manager's style.
Mutual Fund Scheme Performance
A fund outperforms its benchmark by 2% a year on average with a tracking error of 4%. What is its information ratio?
Information ratio = active return / tracking error = 2 / 4 = 0.5.
Mutual Fund Scheme Selection
An investor with a 1-year horizon and low risk appetite should generally prefer
A small cap fund
A sector rotation long-short SIF
A thematic equity fund
A money market or low duration debt fund
Short-horizon, low-risk money is better suited to short-maturity debt funds than to volatile equity strategies.
Mutual Fund Scheme Selection
A first-time investor with ₹2 lakh and low risk tolerance asks to invest in an SIF. What is the correct response?
SIFs are not suitable: the investor is below the ₹10 lakh minimum and the products suit higher risk appetites
Invest the ₹2 lakh in an equity long-short SIF
Invest in an SIF through a weekly SIP of ₹2 lakh
Split the money across two SIF strategies
Non-accredited investors need at least ₹10 lakh to enter SIFs, and their complex strategies suit more experienced, higher-risk investors.
Basics of Derivatives
A derivative is a contract whose value
Is fixed at issue and never changes
Is derived from the value of an underlying asset, index or rate
Depends only on the issuer's credit rating
Is set by the RBI
Derivatives such as futures and options derive their value from underlying assets like stocks, indices or interest rates.
Basics of Derivatives
Compared with OTC derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives
Are customised bilateral contracts
Carry higher counterparty risk
Are not regulated
Are standardised and cleared through a clearing corporation that manages counterparty risk
Exchange-traded contracts have standard terms, and the clearing corporation acts as counterparty to both sides, reducing default risk.
Understanding Index
The Nifty 50 index is constructed using which weighting method?
Price weighting
Equal weighting
Revenue weighting
Free-float market capitalisation weighting
Each constituent's weight is based on its free-float market capitalisation, i.e., shares available for public trading.
Understanding Index
Impact cost of a stock or index basket measures
The cost of executing a transaction relative to the ideal price, reflecting liquidity
The brokerage charged by the broker
The tax paid on the trade
The dividend yield of the index
Impact cost is the percentage markup over the ideal (mid) price incurred when executing a trade; lower impact cost means better liquidity.
Equity Futures and Forwards
A stock trades at ₹1,000 and the risk-free rate is 8% per year. Using simple cost of carry and ignoring dividends, what is the fair price of a 3-month future?
Equity Futures and Forwards
Profits and losses on futures positions are settled every day through
A single settlement only on expiry
Payment of option premium
Daily mark-to-market settlement
Annual reconciliation
Futures are marked to market daily, with gains credited and losses debited to limit build-up of credit risk.
Equity Options
A call option with strike ₹500 trades at a premium of ₹30 when the stock is at ₹520. What is the option's time value?
Intrinsic value = 520 - 500 = ₹20; time value = premium - intrinsic = 30 - 20 = ₹10.
Equity Options
What is the maximum loss for the buyer of a put option?
The premium paid
Unlimited
The strike price
Twice the premium
An option buyer's loss is capped at the premium, because the option can simply be left unexercised.
Strategies Using Equity Futures and Options
A portfolio worth ₹2 crore has a beta of 1.2. Each index futures contract has a value of ₹16 lakh. How many contracts should be sold for a full hedge?
Contracts = (portfolio value x beta) / contract value = (2,00,00,000 x 1.2) / 16,00,000 = 15.
Strategies Using Equity Futures and Options
A trader expects a big move in a stock after results but is unsure of the direction. Which strategy fits?
Short straddle
Covered call
Long straddle (buy a call and a put at the same strike)
Buying futures
A long straddle profits from a large move in either direction, at the cost of both premiums.
Interest Rates and Fixed Income Market
An interest rate of 10% per year compounded semi-annually is equivalent to what effective annual rate?
Interest Rates and Fixed Income Market
If market yields rise after a bond is bought, the bond's price will
Rise
Stay at face value
Fall
Rise only if it is a zero coupon bond
Bond prices and yields move inversely, because future cash flows are discounted at the higher rate.
Interest Rate Derivatives
In a plain vanilla interest rate swap,
Parties exchange the full principal at the start and end
Only one party makes payments
Parties exchange fixed and floating interest payments on a notional principal that is not exchanged
Bonds are physically delivered
Only interest flows (usually netted) are exchanged; the notional amount is used only to compute them.
Interest Rate Derivatives
A Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) is used to
Lock in an interest rate for a future period
Buy shares at a fixed price
Exchange currencies at spot
Insure against default by a borrower
An FRA fixes the rate applicable to a future borrowing or lending period, with only the difference settled.
Exchange Traded Interest Rate Futures
A fund holding a large portfolio of government bonds fears that interest rates will rise. How can it hedge using interest rate futures?
Buy interest rate futures
Buy more long-dated bonds
Sell call options on equities
Sell (short) interest rate futures
Rising rates cut bond prices; a short IRF position gains as futures prices fall, offsetting the portfolio loss.
Exchange Traded Interest Rate Futures
A ₹10 crore bond portfolio has a modified duration of 6. An interest rate futures contract has a value of ₹2 lakh and a modified duration of 7.5. How many contracts are needed for a duration hedge?
Exchange Traded Interest Rate Options
A call option on a bond price (or bond future) gains value when
Interest rates fall
Interest rates rise
Interest rates remain unchanged
Credit spreads widen
Falling rates push bond prices up, so a call on the bond price becomes more valuable.
Exchange Traded Interest Rate Options
A European-style option can be exercised
On any day before expiry
Only on the trade date
Only on the expiry date
Only at the seller's choice
European options allow exercise only at expiry, unlike American options which can be exercised any time up to expiry.
Strategies Using Interest Rate Futures and Options
A speculator who expects interest rates to fall would most likely
Sell interest rate futures
Buy interest rate futures
Buy put options on bond prices
Shorten portfolio duration
Falling rates raise bond and IRF prices, so a long IRF position profits.
Strategies Using Interest Rate Futures and Options
Interest rate futures trade above their fair value based on cost of carry. Which arbitrage locks in a profit?
Sell the bond and buy the futures
Buy both the bond and the futures
Buy the deliverable bond in the cash market and sell the futures
Sell both the bond and the futures
When futures are overpriced, a cash-and-carry arbitrage (buy cash, sell futures) earns the excess over the carry cost.
xii: The main economic role of securities markets is to
Fix interest rates for bank deposits
Channel household savings into productive investment by companies and governments
Securities markets help issuers raise capital from savers and give investors liquidity, supporting capital formation.
Which regulator is primarily responsible for the government securities and money markets?
The RBI regulates government securities, money markets and related instruments; SEBI regulates the broader securities market.
Which entity holds investors' securities in electronic (dematerialised) form?
Depositories (NSDL and CDSL) maintain securities in electronic form, accessed through depository participants.
By acting as counterparty to every trade through novation, a clearing corporation
Guarantees settlement and removes counterparty risk between trading members
Novation makes the clearing corporation the buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer, guaranteeing settlement.
An investor opens a demat account through a
Depository participants are agents of depositories through whom investors open and operate demat accounts.
A key benefit of dematerialisation of securities was that it
Eliminated risks such as forgery, theft and bad delivery of paper certificates
Ended the need for stock exchanges
Electronic holding removed the problems of physical certificates and enabled faster settlement.
An entity raising funds by issuing securities, such as a company or government
Issuers create securities to raise capital; investors buy them, and intermediaries facilitate the process.
Equity shareholders of a company have
A fixed claim to interest payments
A residual claim on profits and assets after all other claims are met
Equity holders are owners and are paid last, which is why equity carries higher risk and higher potential reward.
One advantage of debt financing over equity financing for an issuer is that
Interest need not be paid in losses
Debt never has to be repaid
Interest is tax-deductible and ownership is not diluted
It requires no credit rating ever
Debt keeps ownership intact and interest reduces taxable profit, though it creates fixed payment obligations.
A debenture that can be converted into equity shares at a later date is an example of a
Convertible debentures combine features of debt and equity, making them hybrid instruments.
Compared with equity shareholders, preference shareholders
Have priority in receiving dividends and capital repayment
Receive interest that is tax-deductible for the company
Rank after equity shareholders in liquidation
Preference shares rank ahead of equity for dividends and repayment of capital on winding up.
A bond with face value ₹1,000 and an 8% annual coupon trades at ₹950. What is its current yield?
Restoring the asset mix to its target weights after market movements
Rebalancing sells assets that have grown beyond target and buys those below target, maintaining the intended risk level.
Combining assets whose returns are not perfectly correlated in a portfolio
Low correlation means assets do not all fall together, so diversification lowers portfolio volatility.
Investors often hold gold in a portfolio mainly as
A source of regular coupon income
A hedge against inflation and currency weakness
Gold pays no income but tends to preserve value during inflation and currency depreciation.
A company pays a dividend of ₹12 per share and its share price is ₹400. What is the dividend yield?
Estimating a share's intrinsic value from the company's financial statements, earnings and industry prospects is called
Fundamental analysis studies business and financial data, while technical analysis studies price and volume patterns.
Any sale of shares on the stock exchange
The first offer of shares to the public by an unlisted company
An offer of shares only to existing shareholders
A buyback of shares by a listed company
In an IPO, a company offers shares to the public for the first time and then gets listed.
A Follow-on Public Offer (FPO) is made by
A company that is already listed
A company making its first public issue
A mutual fund launching a scheme
An FPO is a further public issue by a company whose shares are already listed.
In a book-built issue, the cap of the price band can be at most what percentage of the floor price?
SEBI requires the cap to be at least 105% and at most 120% of the floor price.
In a public issue, a retail individual investor is one who applies for shares worth up to
Applications by individuals up to ₹2 lakh fall in the retail individual investor category.
Under ASBA, the investor's application money is
Blocked in the bank account and debited only on allotment
Paid in cash to the broker
Kept by the stock exchange for one month
Application Supported by Blocked Amount keeps funds in the investor's account, earning interest, until allotment.
After a public issue closes, shares must be listed within
SEBI has mandated listing within three working days of the issue closing date (T+3).
A rights issue is an offer of new shares
To the general public through book building
To existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings
Rights issues give existing shareholders the first right to buy, and the rights can usually be renounced.
Who manages the public issue process, including due diligence and preparation of the offer document?
SEBI-registered merchant bankers act as lead managers responsible for managing the issue.
A Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) is a way for
An unlisted company to list on an exchange
Retail investors to buy government bonds
A listed company to raise capital by placing securities with qualified institutional buyers
A mutual fund to launch an NFO

A 10%, 15% or 20% move in Nifty 50 or Sensex triggers a market-wide trading halt.

Margins act as collateral so that adverse price moves do not lead to settlement default.

Physically settled by delivery of shares

The number of trades during the day

Open interest counts positions still open; it rises when new positions are created and falls when they are closed.
